goal: What should our support dashboard help people do?
summary: Illustrative first round. Settle the audience and the first useful outcome; those answers determine the access and workflow questions that follow.

decisions.question: Who is the first version for?
decisions.why: The audience determines which information belongs on the dashboard and which access decisions we need next.

options.label: Our immediate support team
options.detail: Focus on a shared daily workflow with a small group.

options.label: Several internal teams
options.detail: Include handoffs and decide what each team can see.

options.label: Customers as well
options.detail: Customer access adds decisions about data separation and external communication.

decisions.recommendation: Start with the immediate team if the goal is to validate usefulness quickly; expand only when a concrete cross-team need is clear.

decisions.question: Which outcome matters most in the first version?
decisions.why: A clear first outcome helps us judge whether a feature belongs in scope.

options.label: Every issue has a clear owner
options.detail: Find unassigned work and make handoffs visible.

options.label: See which integrations are blocked
options.detail: Prioritize the cases preventing customers from launching.

options.label: Reduce time spent preparing status reports
options.detail: Produce a reliable overview for recurring updates.

decisions.recommendation: Choose the outcome that currently causes the most repeated work or missed follow-up. Ownership is a useful starting point only if that is the main pain.

decisions.question: What information may each audience see?
decisions.why: This depends on the chosen audience; don't assume a shared access model before Q1 is answered.
decisions.recommendation: Decide after Q1. Inspect existing access rules before proposing changes.
